keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «너무 가까이 다가간 것은 빛까지도 빨려 들어가 다시는 나오지 못한다(핵심 특징)» 와 «블랙홀은 과학자들이 중력, 공간, 시간을 이해하도록 돕는다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the key feature (anything that gets too close, even light, is pulled in and can never come out) and the conclusion (black holes help scientists understand gravity, space, and time). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why does a black hole’s gravity become incredibly strong?
opts: Because so much mass is packed so tightly
Because hot gas shines brightly around it
Because it is very close to the Earth
evs: Because so much mass is packed so tightly, its gravity becomes incredibly strong.
Hot gas swirling around a black hole also shines brightly before it falls in.
Do not worry, though; it is much too far away to pull us in.
What if there were a place in space where even light could not escape?
why: 아주 많은 질량이 아주 좁은 곳에 빽빽하게 모여 있어서 중력이 엄청나게 강해진다고 했어요. 우리 은하의 블랙홀은 지구에서 아주 멀리 있어요.
So much mass is packed so tightly that its gravity becomes incredibly strong. The black hole in our galaxy is much too far away to pull us in.

qs.q: In “stars and gas move around an empty-looking area,” what does “empty-looking” mean?
qs.qko: «stars and gas move around an empty-looking area» 에서 «empty-looking» 은 무슨 뜻인가요?
evs: Since no light comes out, black holes are invisible.
In 2019, scientists shared the first picture of a black hole's shadow.
That place is real, and it is called a black hole.
Do not worry, though; it is much too far away to pull us in.
why: 블랙홀에서는 빛이 나오지 않아서 보이지 않는다고 했어요. 그래서 블랙홀이 있는 곳은 «아무것도 없는 것처럼 보이는» 곳이에요. 실제로 비어 있는 것은 아니에요.
No light comes out of a black hole, so it is invisible. The area only looks empty; it is not really empty.

qs.q: How can scientists find a black hole if they cannot see it?
qs.qko: 블랙홀은 보이지 않는데, 과학자들은 어떻게 블랙홀을 찾을 수 있나요?
opts: They watch how stars and gas move around it, and they see hot gas shine before it falls in
They fly a spaceship into it and look around
They listen to it with their own ears
evs: They watch how stars and gas move around an empty-looking area.
Hot gas swirling around a black hole also shines brightly before it falls in.
Anything that gets too close, including light, is pulled in and can never come out.
There is even a giant black hole at the center of our own Milky Way galaxy.
why: 과학자들은 아무것도 없어 보이는 곳 주위에서 별과 가스가 어떻게 움직이는지 살펴봐요. 또 블랙홀 주위를 도는 뜨거운 가스는 빨려 들어가기 전에 밝게 빛나요. 두 문장이 두 가지 단서예요.
Scientists watch how stars and gas move around an empty-looking area, and hot gas swirling around a black hole shines brightly before it falls in. These are two clues.

ends: How are stars born, and how do they die?
How did telescopes around the world work together like one giant telescope?
세계 곳곳의 망원경은 어떻게 하나의 거대한 망원경처럼 힘을 합쳤을까?
A Telescope as Big as Earth
